security_audit.summary: The skill is primarily defensive security documentation with local scanning scripts. Most static findings are false positives caused by intentionally unsafe examples, scanner regexes, or standard audit commands, but several copyable unsafe examples remain confirmed risks for marketplace presentation.

remediation.issue: Copyable vulnerable examples appear in primary documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Keep wrong examples short, clearly label them as non-production, and prefer pseudocode for os.system, pickle.loads, MD5 password hashing, and innerHTML examples.

remediation.issue: A realistic fake API key appears in the secrets section.
remediation.suggestion: Replace secret-shaped values with placeholders such as <API_KEY> so scanners and users do not treat them as real credentials.

remediation.issue: Local shell scripts run several dependency and grep tools.
remediation.suggestion: Document that scripts should be run only on trusted local repositories and review command output before acting on findings.

content.value_statement: Security reviews can miss common web application risks when guidance is scattered. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a focused OWASP-based checklist with examples and local audit scripts.
actual_capabilities: Provides OWASP Top 10 checklists and prevention guidance for web applications.
Explains secure authentication patterns for passwords, sessions, JWT, OAuth, MFA, and lockout.
Documents cryptography patterns for encryption, hashing, signatures, secure randomness, and key storage.
Lists HTTP security header configurations for Flask, FastAPI, Express, and Nginx.
Includes local shell scripts for dependency auditing and grep-based security checks.
limitations: It does not replace a full penetration test or threat model.
The grep-based scanner can miss vulnerabilities and can report false positives.
Some examples show unsafe code for contrast and require careful reading.
Dependency audit scripts depend on external tools installed on the local machine.

use_cases.title: Review a web feature before merge
use_cases.description: Use the OWASP checklist to inspect access control, injection, authentication, logging, and SSRF risks before approving code.

use_cases.title: Harden application defaults
use_cases.description: Apply secure header, session, and cookie guidance when preparing a service for production.

use_cases.title: Teach secure implementation patterns
use_cases.description: Compare unsafe and safer examples for authentication, cryptography, and input handling during code coaching.

prompt_templates.title: Check one feature
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the security-patterns skill to review this feature for OWASP Top 10 risks. Focus on input validation, authorization, and secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Review authentication code
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the authentication patterns to review this login and session code. Check password hashing, cookies, rate limiting, JWT handling, and account lockout.

prompt_templates.title: Audit cryptography choices
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the crypto patterns to evaluate this encryption and signing code. Identify weak algorithms, key storage problems, nonce reuse, and unsafe custom crypto.

prompt_templates.title: Run a structured security pass
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill as a pre-release checklist. Review OWASP risks, security headers, dependency exposure, secrets handling, and provide prioritized remediation steps.

output_examples.input: Review this API endpoint for security risks.
output: Access control needs a server-side owner check before returning the record.
The SQL query should use parameters instead of string formatting.
Add a rate limit if this endpoint can trigger expensive work.
Add a restrictive Content-Security-Policy with default-src self.
Enable HSTS after confirming HTTPS works for all subdomains.
Remove X-Powered-By and test the deployed headers with a scanner.
Use bcrypt, Argon2, or scrypt with a current work factor.
Do not use MD5 or SHA1 for password hashing.
Store reset tokens as hashes and expire them after a short time.

best_practices: Start with the OWASP checklist, then inspect framework-specific details in the reference files.
Treat every unsafe example as a pattern to remove, not a template to copy.
Run dependency and grep scripts only on trusted local repositories and review results manually.
anti_patterns: Do not assume the scanner output is complete or free of false positives.
Do not paste wrong examples into production code without the surrounding warning context.
Do not use the skill as a substitute for testing authorization, authentication, and cryptographic behavior.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps AI assistants review code for common web security issues using OWASP and secure coding patterns.

faq.question: Does it run a full security scanner?
faq.answer: No. It includes simple local scripts, but they are grep and dependency audit helpers.

faq.question: Can it find every vulnerability?
faq.answer: No. It provides structured guidance and examples, but manual review and testing are still required.

faq.question: Are the scripts safe to run?
faq.answer: They run local audit commands and file searches. Run them only in repositories you trust.

faq.question: Why are unsafe examples included?
faq.answer: They show what vulnerable patterns look like so users can recognize and replace them.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
